lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - A Look and learn

details: Look and learn reviews the target structure ‘there is/are’ and singular and plural nouns, covering meaning form & pronunciation.
Look for correct identification of when to add ‘s’ or ‘es’ to a noun and when to use ‘there is’ or ‘there are’.
“Learning English is hard. Let’s use our big brains to try and remember when we use ‘there is’ and when we use ‘there are’.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - B Look and circle

details: Look and circle further practises the target structure with students choosing if each picture shows a singular or plural noun.
Look for accurate identification of singular/plural nouns in the pictures, correct word choice, and neat circling of the answers.
“Our brains are now warmed up. Let’s get them working a bit harder!”

details: Look and learn reviews the prepositions ‘on’, ‘in’ and ‘under’ and strengthens recognition of the target words through the picture examples.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - D Look and write

details: Look and write further reviews the prepositions. Students look at the picture and write the correct preposition to complete the sentences.
Look for accurate identification of objects in the pictures and where they are, correct preposition choice, and correct spelling and neat writing of the answers.
“Our last brain exercise for now. Can you fill in the gaps?”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book pp.110 - 112 - A Choose and trace

details: Choose and trace develops first sound identification. Students say the sounds and match the letters to the picture that begins with that sound.
Look for correct identification of the pictures and their first letters, and consistent letter formation.
“I want to wear a crown and be a queen! Can you help me make the word queen?”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book pp.110 - 112 - A Point and say

details: Point and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Point shows they match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for correct pointing, clear sounds, and confident repetition.
“Here’s a story about me, the queen!. Let’s listen to  it together!”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book pp.110 - 112 - C&D How many words start with v or qu? Circle the words that start with v or qu.

details: This activity strengthens the identification of the first sounds of words, reinforces sound/letter recognition, and reinforces comprehension of the words by linking them to the pictures.
Look for correct number of words beginning with the target letters, and correct circling of the words that begin with those letters.
“Did you like the story about me?”
